correctness.rationale: Affine normalization and character restriction reduce every dimension to the 27-point local cube with multiplicity \(3^{d-3}\). The finite local claim is exact: every four evaluation rows have rank at least three, so any zero set of size at least four contains a rank-three triple determining the coefficient hyperplane. Exhaustive exact Eisenstein arithmetic over all triples shows that every such admissible hyperplane has intersection size three or five, while explicit nonzero coefficient vectors realize zero counts zero, one, two, three, and five. A fresh independent Eisenstein-arithmetic replay in this audit reproduced 216 rank-three triples with three-point intersections and 648 with five-point intersections among all-nonzero cofactor vectors.
correctness.risk: The finite local classification is certificate-based but exact; the theorem applies only to affine rank three.

final_claim: For every affine-independent four-point support in \(\mathbb F_3^d\), \(d\ge3\), the attainable Fourier-support sizes are exactly \(\{22,24,25,26,27\}3^{d-3}\). Equivalently, the normalized affine polynomial \(a_0+a_1X+a_2Y+a_3Z\) with all coefficients nonzero has exactly \(0,1,2,3\), or \(5\) zeros on \(\mu_3^3\), and never four or more than five.
limitations: Only affine-independent four-point supports over \(\mathbb F_3\).
The local 27-point certificate does not by itself cover other characteristics.
